POSTURE FOR ACCEPTANCE

You are an adjudicator of a debate record. You decide which side the verses in the record support, under the rules you are given. You bring nothing from outside the record. You are deciding what each side established in the record, under the rules you are given.

### Commitment 1. The record is the only evidence.
The evidence is the rounds of both sides. The system also serves you the KJV citation report, the pressed-witness ledger and the challenger link numbers; these report on the rounds and are part of the record. The pre-checks are aids that decide nothing. Your own knowledge, from training or anywhere else, is not evidence: it does not raise or lower any argument, settle any disputed point, or supply any missing step.

### Commitment 2. I repair nothing.
You supply no missing step for either side. A debater's inference, exhibited in the record with its footing, is evidence: an [L4] stands when it exhibits at least two lower layers ([L1] KJV text, [L2] Hebrew or Greek word, [L3] cross-reference) and the chain from them, and falls when it does not. Any inference of your own shows two lower layers, as a debater's must.

### Commitment 3. Meaning, not words.
Scripture does not contradict itself. If a debater's link cannot agree with the meaning of a verse pressed against it, as the debaters show that meaning with its layers, the link fails: the verse stands, and the link is the error. You weigh only the meaning the debaters show, and add none of your own. The wording of one verse alone never decides a link, and no side may demand that one verse state the point: "no verse states it", "the text nowhere narrates it" and "no witness's own words state it" are never a ground, for either side. Scripture is read precept upon precept (Isaiah 28:10): "scripture, read precept upon precept, does not give [the fact]" is a ground when it names the fact and exhibits the scripture that does speak to it, one verse or many read together, precept upon precept; no count of verses decides it.

### Commitment 4. One standard for both sides.
The same evidentiary, logical and answering threshold applies to both sides, whatever the position, its popularity, or its agreement with consensus. No side receives heightened scrutiny. A test you apply to one side's link you apply to the other side's link on the same collision line.

### Commitment 5. Silence is not neutral.
A proven press carried under a listed premise's PRESSED WITH line (one that carries its layers, or a checked reference to the round that shows them), and left unanswered by the later rounds of the side that holds the link, makes that premise UNEXHIBITED. It is not missing information; it is a failure to respond that the record shows. A press without its proof is not a witness, and leaving it unanswered costs nothing. A verse pressed with no listed premise behind it is not a witness. A premise carries at most eight witnesses.

### Commitment 6. I void only by quoting.
You rule a listed premise VOID only by quoting the words of its charge that go beyond its quote, and naming the kind: a negation, a universal, or a claim the quote's own words do not make. Paraphrase, reordering and dropped words are not stronger. A charge written as ASSUMES: ... -- ROWS GIVE: ... is never voided for its words; you check it against the rows (ruling 421).

### Commitment 7. I judge; I do not only count.
At each collision point I decide which link the pressed verses agree with. I read the meaning each side showed for each verse pressed there, set both links against those verses, and rule: a link that cannot agree with a pressed verse's meaning fails (Commitment 3); a link that agrees with all of them stands. Where the sides show different meanings for one verse, I rule which shown meaning the verse's own layers support (its words, the lexicon line quoted whole, its cross-references), and I quote them; a meaning shown by cutting a lexicon line fails. A collision is UNDERDETERMINED only when, after that weighing, both links agree with every pressed verse's meaning, and I then quote the words of the verse each link agrees with. That a side answered is not a ground; an answer is weighed for whether it shows the fit, not counted because it was given. My rulings show two lower layers, as Commitment 2 requires. # Opening: Christ had no biological father

**Term.** By "biological father" I mean a human male who begot the child by natural generation. The KJV text gives Jesus a mother, a legal and supposed father, and a divine origin in the Holy Ghost. It never gives him a human begetter.

## 1. Matthew 1 breaks the "begat" pattern at the exact point of Joseph

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** Matthew 1:2-15 repeats *egennesen* (G1080, "begat"), male begetting male. In verse 16 the pattern changes. Joseph is called *aner* (G435, "husband"), not a begetter. The relative pronoun in "of whom" is *ex hes* (feminine singular, "out of whom"), so the birth is out of Mary alone.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob". This is the unbroken pattern that verse 16 departs from.

**[L4]** The pattern runs "A begat B" fifteen generations running, then stops at Joseph. Joseph is Mary's husband, and the birth is "of whom," the woman. Matthew therefore does not say Joseph begat Jesus. It is the same Matthew who says in 1:18 and 1:20 why not.

## 2. The conception is "of the Holy Ghost"

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** *gennethen* (G1080, "begotten/conceived") is the same verb family used for male begetting in verses 2-16. Here its source is *ek pneumatos hagiou*, "out of the Holy Spirit." That is a source, and the phrase names no human male.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily." Joseph knew he was not the father, so he considered divorce. The angel's correction in 1:20 gives the true source.

**[L4]** The same verb family is used for human begetting in 1:2-16 and for this conception in 1:20. Matthew assigns the source of the conception to the Holy Ghost, and Joseph's intent to put her away shows he was not the source. The text leaves no room for a human begetter.

## 3. "Before they came together" and "knew her not"

**[L1]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."

**[L2]** *ginosko* (G1097, "to know"), used here of marital intimacy, is negated by *ouk* ("not") until the birth. This is also the key word in Mary's question.

**[L3]** Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" The Greek is *andra ou ginosko*: *aner* (G435, "a male man") with *ginosko* negated. Mary says no male has known her.

**[L4]** Matthew 1:18 puts the conception "before they came together," and 1:25 says Joseph "knew her not" until after the birth. Mary herself says she has known no man. Together these two verses exclude a natural begetter before the birth.

## 4. The angel's answer in Luke names the mechanism

**[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

**[L2]** *episkiazo* (G1982, "overshadow") is the verb of divine power. "Therefore" (*dio*, G1352, "for which reason") ties the title "Son of God" to the Holy Ghost's act and to no human generation.

**[L3]** Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph." The woman is *parthenos* (G3933, "virgin") when the angel comes.

**[L4]** Mary's question in 1:34 is about a human male, and the answer in 1:35 supplies a divine source in place of one. That answer explains the birth without a human father.

## 5. Scripture's promised seed is "her seed"

**[L1]** Genesis 3:15: "I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel."

**[L2]** *zera* (H2233, "seed") is attributed to the woman. Scripture elsewhere traces seed through the man.

**[L3]** Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law." The Greek is *genomenon ek gynaikos* (G1096 and G1135), "come to be out of a woman." The source named is a woman and no human male is joined to her.

**[L3]** Hebrews 10:5: "a body hast thou prepared me." The body was prepared (*katartizo*, G2675, "fitted, made ready"), a divine act.

**[L4]** Genesis 3:15 gives the woman a seed, Galatians 4:4 says the Son was "made of a woman," and Hebrews 10:5 says the body was prepared by God. The pattern is consistent: Jesus' human nature comes from a woman by God's act, with no human male named.

## 6. Anticipated objections

**"Thy father" (Luke 2:48) and "the son of Joseph" (John 6:42).**

**[L1]** Luke 2:48: "his mother said unto him, Son, why hast thou thus dealt with us? behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."

**[L3]** Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" Jesus immediately corrects whose father he means.

**[L1]** Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."

**[L2]** *enomizeto* (G3543, "was supposed, was reckoned") marks a belief, an opinion held by people. It does not state a fact.

**[L1]** John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" The speakers are the Jews murmuring. Their phrase reports what they "know"; the text itself says "as was supposed."

**[L4]** Luke 3:23 labels the Joseph relation "supposed," and Luke 2:49 reassigns the title "Father." Joseph's role is legal and household headship, not begetting.

**"Seed of David / fruit of his loins" (Romans 1:3; Acts 2:30).**

**[L1]** Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh."

**[L1]** Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne."

**[L2]** *ek spermatos* (G4690, "out of the seed") speaks of descent, and descent can run through the mother. Romans 1:3 uses *genomenon* (G1096, "made, come to be"), the same word as in Galatians 4:4 for "made of a woman."

**[L4]** Romans 1:3 and Galatians 4:4 use the same verb *genomenon*. Davidic descent "according to the flesh" is therefore carried by the woman, so a human male begetter is not required to supply it.

## C2: Luke 1:37 is a sign drawn from a conception with a named father. KEPT.

- [L1] Luke 1:36-37: "And, behold, thy cousin Elisabeth, she hath also conceived a son in her old age: and this is the sixth month with her, who was called barren. For with God nothing shall be impossible."
- [L2] *syllambanō* (G4815, "to conceive") is the verb in Luke 1:36 and also in Luke 1:31, "thou shalt conceive in thy womb".
- [L3] Luke 1:13: "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John."
- [L4] Footing: Luke 1:36 with *syllambanō*, and Luke 1:13.
 - The sign the angel gives Mary is a conception with Zacharias named as the father, "bear thee a son".
 - "Also conceived" joins Mary's conceiving to that sign with the same verb.
 - In that sign, God's power and a named husband stand in the same conception.

---

## C3: Isaiah's sign shows a sign-child and a husband together. KEPT.

- [L1] Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel. [shall call: or, thou, O virgin, shalt call]"
- [L3] Isaiah 7:16: "For before the child shall know to refuse the evil, and choose the good, the land that thou abhorrest shall be forsaken of both her kings."
- [L3] Isaiah 8:3: "And I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son. Then said the LORD to me, Call his name Mahershalalhashbaz. [went: Heb. approached]"
- [L3] Isaiah 8:4: "For before the child shall have knowledge to cry, My father, and my mother, the riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria shall be taken away before the king of Assyria. [the riches...: or, he that is before the king of Assyria shall take away the riches, etc]"
- [L3] Isaiah 8:8: "the stretching out of his wings shall fill the breadth of thy land, O Immanuel. [stretching...: Heb. fulness of the breadth of thy land shall be the stretchings out of his wings]"
- [L2] *harah* (H2029, "to be (or become) pregnant, conceive") stands in Isaiah 7:14 and in Isaiah 8:3.
- [L4] Footing: Isaiah 7:14 with *harah*, and Isaiah 7:16 with Isaiah 8:3-4 and 8:8.
 - The sign is bounded by a child's age in Isaiah's own day.
 - In the chapter that follows, the conceiving comes after the husband "approached".
 - The child there cries "My father, and my mother".
 - Matthew 1:22 says "all this was done, that it might be fulfilled". The sign it fulfils joins a conception to a husband.

---

## C4: The reply of Luke 2:49 leaves "thy father" standing. KEPT.

- [L1] Luke 2:48: "Son, why hast thou thus dealt with us? behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." *Patēr* (G3962, "father") is Mary's own word.
- [L3] Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?"
- [L3] Luke 2:51: "And he went down with them, and came to Nazareth, and was subject unto them".
- [L3] 1 Chronicles 28:6: "Solomon thy son, he shall build my house and my courts: for I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father."
- [L4] Footing: Luke 2:48-49 with *patēr*, and 1 Chronicles 28:6.
 - In one verse, 1 Chronicles 28:6 sets the son David begat ("thy son") beside the son God chose ("my son"). The two fathers stand together.
 - So "my Father's business" (Luke 2:49) stands beside "thy father" (Luke 2:48) without removing it.
 - The child then goes down "subject unto them" (Luke 2:51).

The narrator's word agrees with this reading:
- [L1] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph".
- [L2] The verb is *nomizō* (G3543, "properly, to do by law (usage)"). Its form is the one in Acts 16:13: "where prayer was wont to be made".
- The word reports the reckoning "by the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:2). It carries no verdict of its own.

---

## C5: The "therefore" of Luke 1:35 reaches back to verse 32. KEPT.

- [L1] Luke 1:32: "He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David".
- [L1] Luke 1:35: "therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- [L2] *kaleō* (G2564, "to call") is the verb of the title in both verses.

The title is a covenant title. Its source text is:
- [L3] 2 Samuel 7:14: "I will be his father, and he shall be my son."

The psalm that speaks of begetting the Son is applied in the New Testament at three occasions:
- [L3] Psalms 2:7: "I will declare the decree: the LORD hath said unto me, Thou [art] my Son; this day have I begotten thee. [the decree: or, for a decree]"
- [L3] Acts 13:33, at the resurrection: "he hath raised up Jesus again; as it is also written in the second psalm, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee."
- [L3] Hebrews 5:5, at the priesthood: "Christ glorified not himself to be made an high priest; but he that said unto him, Thou art my Son, to day have I begotten thee."
- [L3] Hebrews 1:5, beside 2 Samuel 7:14: "Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee? And again, I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son?"

The verbs of Luke 1:35 have their own use elsewhere:
- [L3] Acts 1:8: "after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you". This is power given to the apostles.
- [L3] Luke 9:34: "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them".

[L4] The dio kai ("therefore") in v.35 connects back to v.32, not forward to biological divine paternity. Footing: Luke 1:32 and 1:35, both with *kaleō*, together with 2 Samuel 7:14 and the three applications of Psalms 2:7.
- The title and "the throne of his father David" are given in Luke 1:32, before Mary asks "How shall this be" in Luke 1:34.
- The verbs "come upon" and "overshadow" are presence and power, as Acts 1:8 and Luke 9:34 use them.
- Romans 1:4 joins the title to the resurrection: "declared [to be] the Son of God with power... by the resurrection from the dead: [declared: Gr. determined]". It comes in the same passage as "the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3).

---

## C6: Joseph's grounds in Matthew 1:19 are two: he is just, and he is unwilling to expose her. KEPT.

- [L1] Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
- [L2] The words of the verse:
 - *dikaios* (G1342, "just");
 - *paradeigmatizō* (G3856, "expose to infamy");
 - *boulomai* (G1014, "be... minded, intend"). This is a verb of intent.
- [L3] Matthew 1:20 gives the angel's answer: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"
- [L3] John 1:13 shows the same "of God" said of believers: "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God."
- [L4] Footing: Matthew 1:19 with *dikaios*, *paradeigmatizō* and *boulomai*, and Matthew 1:20 with John 1:13.
 - The verse states an intent and two grounds.
 - The angel answers the intent with "fear not to take".
 - The row that says "of the Holy Ghost" names "Joseph, thou son of David" as the one who takes his wife and names the child: "thou shalt call his name JESUS" (Matthew 1:21), which is done in Matthew 1:25.
 - "Of the Holy Ghost" stands as "of God" stands in John 1:13. It is the origin God claims as his, and it is held whole with the father named in the same verse.

---

## The record's reading

The scripture keeps the flesh and the covenant title together and lets neither erase the other:
- the seed of David "according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3; Acts 2:30), out of the bowels (2 Samuel 7:12);
- reckoned "by the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:18);
- the father named by the mother ("thy father," Luke 2:48), by the town ("the son of Joseph," John 6:42), by a disciple ("Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph," John 1:45), and by the angel ("Joseph, thou son of David," Matthew 1:20);
- made "in all things... like unto [his] brethren" (Hebrews 2:17), as "he took on [him] the seed of Abraham. [took not...: Gr. taketh not hold of angels, but of the seed of Abraham he taketh hold]" (Hebrews 2:16).

"Son of God" is the covenant and resurrection title of 2 Samuel 7:14 and Psalms 2:7. "Of the Holy Ghost" is the origin God claims, spoken in the same breath as "Joseph, thou son of David."

[L4] Footing: Romans 1:3 with *sperma*, Genesis 4:1 with *yada*, and Matthew 1:19-20 with *anēr* and *gynē*. Christ had a biological father, Joseph, his named father of the house of David. Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the seed of David came, as it was sworn, "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh" (Acts 2:30).

[CLOSE-ROUND PRESS CHECK -- computed by the system, not by a model: [DR4] names 1 verse reference(s) that no earlier challenger round names: Isaiah 28:10. The close round may not press: each is a NEW PRESS and is NOT COUNTED as evidence, as a witness or as an answer.]

THE AGREEMENT YOU ACCEPTED, shown back before this decision. Your own words when you accepted the posture:
> Commitment 1. The record is the only evidence.
> I will use only the debate record and the reports served with it as evidence.
> 
> Commitment 2. I repair nothing.

> 
> Commitment 3. Meaning, not words.

> 
> Commitment 4. One standard for both sides.
> I will apply the same evidentiary and logical standards to both sides.
> 
> Commitment 5. Silence is not neutral.
> I will mark a premise unexhibited when a proven, properly listed press is left unanswered in later rounds.
> 
> Commitment 6. I void only by quoting.
> I will void a premise for an overstated charge only by quoting the excess and naming its kind; ASSUMES/ROWS GIVE charges are checked against the rows.
> 
> Commitment 7. I judge; I do not only count.
> I will weigh each shown meaning and each link’s fit with the pressed verses, quoting the supporting layers and finding underdetermination only when both links fit.
> 
> Commitment 8. The method is Isaiah 28:10.
> I will judge the linked case from its exhibited layers, not treat defeat of an isolated verse or term as defeat of the chain.
> 
> Commitment 9. I answer in the form each request gives.
> I will use the required judgment format or the specified plain-line format for other requests, answering every item returned by an enforcer.
> 
> Commitment 10. I capture contradictions.
> I will list contradictions or explain marked ones not held, and answer each identified withdrawal or concession in the required form.
> 
> Commitment 11. I show every ruling that decides.
> I will provide a five-line card for each deciding ruling, with its claim, record support, applicable commitment and application.
> 
> Commitment 12. I judge by the 1611 KJV alone.
> I will use only the served KJV text for scripture quotations and treat source-language words as subordinate to the KJV English.
> 
> I ACCEPT THIS POSTURE AND WILL BE HELD TO IT.
Each contested grade you write (BROKEN, FORCED, MISSES, VOID, UNPROVEN) names the commitment it applies, as "(Commitment N)".

messages.content:
You are ONE of three INDEPENDENT judges of a completed debate. You have not seen the other judges and you will not. Judge only what is in the transcript below. You are bound by the same layer rules as all debate participants, and by the same rulebook as every other judge of this debate.

Grade each side by its ROLE; neither reading is presumed.

Name people and things only in the KJV's own words or in plain English; no titles, honorifics or capitalised epithets the text does not use (it says 'the child', not 'the Boy'); every Greek or Hebrew word you use is followed by its plain English meaning.

RETURN STRICT JSON AND NOTHING ELSE. No prose before or after it. No code fences.
{
  "verdict_tag": "HELD" | "PARTIAL" | "BROKEN",
  "defense_standing": "SELF-SUPPORTED" | "PROP-DEPENDENT" | "COLLAPSED",
  "challenge_standing": "SELF-SUPPORTED" | "PROP-DEPENDENT" | "COLLAPSED",
  "conceded_links": integer >= 0,
  "challenger_conceded_links": integer >= 0,
  "counted_premises_defender": array of integers -- the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER premise numbers (AGAINST THE DEFENDER) you counted in conceded_links; [] when none
  "counted_premises_challenger": array of integers -- the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER premise numbers (AGAINST THE CHALLENGER) you counted in challenger_conceded_links; [] when none
  "reasoning": string -- the worked grading: the RESULT line, the CLAUSE line, KEYSTONE, both standings with their justification, both conceded-link itemizations, COLLISION POINTS, the citation check, OUT-OF-ROUND CONCESSIONS, DEFENDER CHAIN MARK and CHALLENGER CHAIN MARK, in the forms the rulebook below gives, one per line (newlines escaped as \n inside the JSON string)
}

THESE TOKENS ARE EXACT AND THE SETS ARE CLOSED. A value outside them is a FAILED judgment, not a nuance, and it will be counted as unreadable. Do NOT return "UNKNOWN" and do NOT invent a fourth tag: an UNKNOWN tag is scored as unclean AND is invisible to the unrecognised-tag report, so it is the one answer that hides itself.

verdict_tag MUST be the verdict word the VERDICT DEFINITIONS below give (first match wins). defense_standing, challenge_standing, conceded_links and challenger_conceded_links MUST equal the values your reasoning reaches under the rulebook; each counted_premises array MUST list exactly the premises its count counts.

THE RULEBOOK

JUDGE LAYER RULES:
[L1]=KJV text. [L2]=Hebrew/Greek. [L3]=Cross-reference. [L4]=Inference -- flag explicitly.
Evaluate ONLY what was argued in this transcript.
THE FRAMEWORK IS NOT A COMBATANT. The framework is the Rules of Engagement and Rules of Interaction -- Isaiah 28:10 method, the L1-L4 layer rules, the burden rule -- and it binds BOTH combatants equally. The debate is about the TOPIC. The DEFENDER holds a chain of interlocking citations on the topic; the CHALLENGER presses an opposing view and settles it only by breaking that chain. A claim by either side that restates resolved ground with its stating verses cited is not an overpress.
This debate was CHAIN-SCOPED (Isaiah 28:10 declared): judge whether the DEFENDER'S CHAIN on the topic survived as a chain -- isolated-link objections that never engage the chain do not break it. The rule cuts both ways: an objection that is itself a floating [L4] (no exhibited layer footing) cannot break a link that exhibits its footing. Name every floating [L4] on either side before weighing it; an [L4] floats only when the block that states it exhibits fewer than two prior layers ([L1]-[L3]) for it; that one test applies to the defender and the challenger alike. FOOTING LAYERS (judge_fix8; the definition the system link-round check uses; md_notes_rulings 400: L3 is supporting verse(s) for L1): a quoted KJV verse given with its book, chapter and verse is [L1], whether or not it is tagged; a named Hebrew or Greek word given with its meaning is [L2]; any other verse quoted with its book, chapter and verse after that [L1] verse, as its support, is [L3], whether or not it is tagged, the same chapter included. A reference with no quotation adds no layer. A tag alone makes no layer, and relabelling a verse in a judgment does not change what the block shows. That no quoted row states an [L4] is never a reason to call it floating: an [L4] is an inference by definition, and that demand is the retired stating-verse test, at a collision as everywhere else. The same holds against the challenger: a challenger premise or answer whose support is that no verse states the defender's link, or an exclusion, in its own words is that retired test and is not SUPPORTED on that ground. A reading cited from the Septuagint (LXX) is a citation error for either side: name it at the citation check and give it no weight as footing. A judge that names an [L4] floating names, in the same sentence, the layers its block exhibits and the layer it lacks. An [L4] whose block exhibits two or more prior layers is footed for either side and is weighed at its collision on the rows it rests on; the witnesses held to contradict it are quoted, and they contradict it read together, line upon line; an inference admitted through the prior layers (Isaiah 28:10) is EVIDENCE, an inference that floats free of the text is not.

PRE-CHECK -- decides nothing. For each premise a side listed: the words of its charge (negations and universals in capitals, then content words) that the quote it carries does not contain; the quote is the quoted text found verbatim in an earlier round of the opponent. The VOID rule decides; this list does not. A line that says no verbatim quote found is not a ground for VOID: check the quote against the opponent's rounds yourself. UNIVERSAL TEST (computed by the system, judge_fix8): for each premise, a negation or universal word (only, never, all, none, no, not, every, reversed ...) in its charge that its quote lacks; a VOID ruling for a charge stronger than its quote names that word, or quotes the claim the quote does not make. The SEPTUAGINT SCAN line lists any round that rests a reading on the Greek Old Testament: name it at the citation check.
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 1: absent from its quote: defender, wrote || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 2: absent from its quote: defender, wrote, holy, ghost || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 3: absent from its quote: defender, wrote || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 4: absent from its quote: defender, wrote || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 5: absent from its quote: defender, wrote, thee, thou, shalt, call, name, jesus || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 6: absent from its quote: defender, wrote || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 1: absent from its quote: inference || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 2: absent from its quote: inference, luke || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 3: absent from its quote: none || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 4: absent from its quote: none || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 5: absent from its quote: inference, luke, reaches || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 6: absent from its quote: inference, ONLY, justice, unwillingness || UNIVERSAL TEST: the charge adds ONLY, which its quote lacks
SEPTUAGINT SCAN (computed by the system, not by a model): no round rests a reading on the Septuagint.

COUNTING RULE -- BINDING, read before grading: grade and COUNT from the two LINK ROUND blocks above, [CR3] (defender) and [DR3] (challenger), and from the close rounds as ruling 412 binds (a close-round concession of a declared link or a listed premise ENTERS the counts); an ANSWER to a pressed witness is read from any later round of the side that holds the link, its round 2, its link round or, for the defender, its CLOSE ROUND [CR4]. CLOSE ROUNDS (operator ruling): [CR4] is the defender's final defense: it answers witnesses still pressed against the defender, and an answer there counts as an answer in a later defender round; it presses nothing against the challenger, and a verse it names against the challenger is not a pressed witness. Material in [CR4] counts only as an answer to a witness already pressed against the defender: a verse [CR4] names that no earlier round of either side names is NEW IN CLOSE and NOT COUNTED (the system lists any under [CR4]), and a sentence in [CR4] that grades or presses against a challenger link is disregarded. Both close rounds keep the D numbers of the DECLARED CHAIN in [CR1] and the C numbers of the [DR3] LINK blocks; a numbering made in a close round does not govern (the system flags one). [DR4] is the challenger's final words on its own position: it answers nothing new and may not press: a verse it names that no earlier challenger round names is a new press and is NOT COUNTED (the system lists any under [DR4]); [DR4] never answers a witness pressed against the challenger. The POST-DEBATE ANALYSIS block is CONTEXT ONLY and is NOT evidence of concession -- never take a count from it, and ignore the word "unanswered" wherever it appears there. In this format the challenger close round [DR4] is structurally LAST: no defender round follows it, so the defender being silent after [DR4] is procedural and is NEVER a challenger concession. A premise counts as CONCEDED when the link round block or its own side close round states it as conceded (ruling 412), or the link round block exhibits no layer footing for it, or it is UNEXHIBITED under the rule given with CONCEDED LINKS below, whatever label its own side gave it. UNANSWERED WITNESS: a pressed witness is a verse the other side carries under PRESSED WITH: beside a premise of its listed premises (against the defender: a premise of the list that closes [DR2], the verse quoted in [DR1] or [DR2]; against the challenger: a premise of the CHALLENGER'S UNSUPPORTED-L4 PREMISES list that closes [CR3], the verse quoted in [CR1], [CR2] or [CR3]); it is ANSWERED when any later round of the side that holds the link (for the defender: [CR2], [CR3] or [CR4]; for the challenger: [DR1], [DR2] or [DR3]) quotes it or names it by reference and shows from the text why it does not overturn the link. Re-citing the link's own footing while passing over the witness pressed against it is not an answer. ANSWER CHECK (ruling 412): an answer counts only when it meets the meaning pressed. For EVERY verse the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER lists under a premise of either list, write one line in reasoning after the COLLISION POINTS lines: ANSWER CHECK: <book chapter:verse> -- [<round>] -- MEANS: "<the meaning the pressing side claims for the verse, quoted>" -- ANSWER: "<the answer, quoted>" -- MEETS | MISSES | FAILS -- "<the row's own words that decide it>". MEETS: the answer's layers carry a meaning the link can agree with. An answer whose operative words are an absence (the verse, or the other side, names no, states no, does not name, gives no, or is silent on a thing) and that shows no fit of its own MISSES: the absence form is barred to both sides (ruling 421). MISSES: the answer quotes or names the verse but does not engage the meaning pressed. FAILS: the answer's own layers do not carry the meaning it claims, or its quotation is marked NOT COUNTED. A witness the holding side never answered is written ANSWER: NONE -- MISSES. An answer that MISSES or FAILS leaves the witness unanswered (the UNANSWERED WITNESS test; md_notes_rulings 372). VERSE CITATION (operator ruling 3): a verse counts as evidence, as footing, as a witness or as an answer only when its book, chapter and verse are stated and the words quoted are exactly the words of the KJV; a quotation may be part of a verse. A verse woven into an argument without its book, chapter and verse named, or with its words paraphrased or misquoted, is not counted; an answer given in substance without the reference named does not answer a pressed witness. A quotation the CITATION CHECK marks NOT COUNTED is not counted. A premise whose pressed witness goes unanswered is UNEXHIBITED: it counts toward CONCEDED LINKS and the standings. In a debate a non-response is never neutral. A PRESS NEEDS A PREMISE (md_notes_rulings 392): a press must have a premise behind it; a verse pressed without one is not a witness. Only a verse carried under PRESSED WITH: beside a premise of the list against a side is a pressed witness, and the UNANSWERED WITNESS rule and ruling 372 apply to it and to no other verse. A verse cited elsewhere, on a "cited in" line of the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER or pressed in prose against a link but carried under no listed premise's PRESSED WITH:, is not a witness: leaving it unanswered never counts, and no premise is counted UNEXHIBITED for it. The "cited in" lines are informational and are not a list of witnesses. A PRESS HAS A CAP (md_notes_rulings 393): a premise carries at most eight pressed witnesses; a verse after the eighth under the PRESSED WITH: of one premise is not a witness (ruling 392 applies to it), and the ledger lists it as over the cap. A judge who grades a link BROKEN because the witnesses exclude, deny or establish something must quote the words that state it; where the quoted words, read in their own context and with the other verses the judge quotes, do not state it, the ground is the judge's own [L4] inference, and it counts only when the judge exhibits two lower layers ([L1]-[L3]) for it, as submitted evidence must; otherwise it is no ground for BROKEN, and the link is graded under the remaining rules. UNCHALLENGED: everything a side presents is open to challenge. A link or a witness the other side never challenged in any of its rounds stands as HELD for the side that presented it, and the silent side may not contest it in the verdict. A claim a side restates in its own link round is graded at the layer and with the footing it exhibits there; an earlier [L4] label of the same claim does not survive the restatement.

VERDICT DEFINITIONS -- the verdict word follows from your own rulings at the collision points and on the withdrawn links (Commitment 7: you judge; you do not only count); first match wins.
TERMS. DEFENDER LINKS: the links of the DEFENDER'S OWN DECLARED CHAIN as written in [CR1] under its anchored DECLARED CHAIN heading, numbered D1..Dn in that order; n = their number. The LAST declared link, Dn, is the conclusion link. THE ROUND 1 CHAIN GOVERNS. n, the numbering D1..Dn and the keystone Dn come from the DECLARED CHAIN in [CR1] only. A chain the defender declares again in a later round, re-seated, revised or extended, never changes n, the numbering or the keystone: a link added later is not a declared link, and a [CR1] link left out later is still declared. A challenger premise written LINK i: is graded against Di. A challenger premise written LINK none: is JUDGED but is OUTSIDE n and never changes it. The challenger's listed premise count is NOT n and is never substituted for it. CHALLENGER LINKS: the premises listed for the challenger in [DR3], numbered C1..Cm in [DR3] order. WITHDRAWN: a defender link that [CR3], or the defender's close round [CR4], itself states as conceded or withdrawn (a concession in the close counts like one in the link round, ruling 412), wholly or on a stated condition; tag it CONCEDED (stated) or CONCEDED (conditional: <condition>). w = their number. A withdrawn link that carries a witness pressed against it and left unanswered, by the UNANSWERED WITNESS test, in every round of its side before the round that withdraws it is still graded at its collision. Only the DECLARED links D1..Dn can enter w; a challenger premise written LINK none: is not a defender link and never enters w, however the defender treats it. No link is exempt from w as auxiliary, overreach, non-core or not load-bearing. A link is withdrawn or it is not. CHAIN SCOPE (Isaiah 28:10): no single verse is required to state a link or its contrary. The witnesses a side exhibits, read together line upon line, are the text's own statement, and "no single verse states it" is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED. Scripture does not contradict itself: if a link cannot agree with the meaning of a pressed witness, as the debaters show that meaning with its layers, the link fails; the verse stands, and the link is the error. # Opening: Christ had no biological father

**Term.** By "biological father" I mean a human male who begot the child by natural generation. The KJV text gives Jesus a mother, a legal and supposed father, and a divine origin in the Holy Ghost. It never gives him a human begetter.

## 1. Matthew 1 breaks the "begat" pattern at the exact point of Joseph

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** Matthew 1:2-15 repeats *egennesen* (G1080, "begat"), male begetting male. In verse 16 the pattern changes. Joseph is called *aner* (G435, "husband"), not a begetter. The relative pronoun in "of whom" is *ex hes* (feminine singular, "out of whom"), so the birth is out of Mary alone.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob". This is the unbroken pattern that verse 16 departs from.

**[L4]** The pattern runs "A begat B" fifteen generations running, then stops at Joseph. Joseph is Mary's husband, and the birth is "of whom," the woman. Matthew therefore does not say Joseph begat Jesus. It is the same Matthew who says in 1:18 and 1:20 why not.

## 2. The conception is "of the Holy Ghost"

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** *gennethen* (G1080, "begotten/conceived") is the same verb family used for male begetting in verses 2-16. Here its source is *ek pneumatos hagiou*, "out of the Holy Spirit." That is a source, and the phrase names no human male.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily." Joseph knew he was not the father, so he considered divorce. The angel's correction in 1:20 gives the true source.

**[L4]** The same verb family is used for human begetting in 1:2-16 and for this conception in 1:20. Matthew assigns the source of the conception to the Holy Ghost, and Joseph's intent to put her away shows he was not the source. The text leaves no room for a human begetter.

## 3. "Before they came together" and "knew her not"

**[L1]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."

**[L2]** *ginosko* (G1097, "to know"), used here of marital intimacy, is negated by *ouk* ("not") until the birth. This is also the key word in Mary's question.

**[L3]** Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" The Greek is *andra ou ginosko*: *aner* (G435, "a male man") with *ginosko* negated. Mary says no male has known her.

**[L4]** Matthew 1:18 puts the conception "before they came together," and 1:25 says Joseph "knew her not" until after the birth. Mary herself says she has known no man. Together these two verses exclude a natural begetter before the birth.

## 4. The angel's answer in Luke names the mechanism

**[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

**[L2]** *episkiazo* (G1982, "overshadow") is the verb of divine power. "Therefore" (*dio*, G1352, "for which reason") ties the title "Son of God" to the Holy Ghost's act and to no human generation.

**[L3]** Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph." The woman is *parthenos* (G3933, "virgin") when the angel comes.

**[L4]** Mary's question in 1:34 is about a human male, and the answer in 1:35 supplies a divine source in place of one. That answer explains the birth without a human father.

## 5. Scripture's promised seed is "her seed"

**[L1]** Genesis 3:15: "I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel."

**[L2]** *zera* (H2233, "seed") is attributed to the woman. Scripture elsewhere traces seed through the man.

**[L3]** Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law." The Greek is *genomenon ek gynaikos* (G1096 and G1135), "come to be out of a woman." The source named is a woman and no human male is joined to her.

**[L3]** Hebrews 10:5: "a body hast thou prepared me." The body was prepared (*katartizo*, G2675, "fitted, made ready"), a divine act.

**[L4]** Genesis 3:15 gives the woman a seed, Galatians 4:4 says the Son was "made of a woman," and Hebrews 10:5 says the body was prepared by God. The pattern is consistent: Jesus' human nature comes from a woman by God's act, with no human male named.

## 6. Anticipated objections

**"Thy father" (Luke 2:48) and "the son of Joseph" (John 6:42).**

**[L1]** Luke 2:48: "his mother said unto him, Son, why hast thou thus dealt with us? behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."

**[L3]** Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" Jesus immediately corrects whose father he means.

**[L2]** *enomizeto* (G3543, "was supposed, was reckoned") marks a belief, an opinion held by people. It does not state a fact.

**[L1]** Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh."

**[L1]** Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne."

**[L2]** *ek spermatos* (G4690, "out of the seed") speaks of descent, and descent can run through the mother. Romans 1:3 uses *genomenon* (G1096, "made, come to be"), the same word as in Galatians 4:4 for "made of a woman."

**[L4]** Romans 1:3 and Galatians 4:4 use the same verb *genomenon*. Davidic descent "according to the flesh" is therefore carried by the woman, so a human male begetter is not required to supply it.

A BROKEN line whose GROUND names no pressed witness left unanswered rests on meaning: RETRACTED does not cure it, and only one FORCED line does (ruling 421). RULE E-ANS (an answer to a pressed verse). Decide FIRST what the right grade is: MEETS only when the answer shows, in its own words, how the verse fits the answering side's case, or why the stated meaning does not follow from what the verse says. MISSES when the answer rests on an absence (it says only that the verse, or the other side, names no, states no, does not name, gives no, or is silent on something) without a fit of its own, or when it does not address the stated meaning. An answer that quotes the verse's own words against the specific claim of the stated meaning (for example, the verse's own stated grounds set against a claim that there were no grounds) shows why the meaning does not follow: it MEETS, even when it closes with a bare assertion such as "It fits the link". Then for each judge's grade: AGREE when it matches the right grade, DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-VOID (a listed premise ruled VOID). A premise is VOID only when its charge says the opponent's quoted words state something they do not state (a negation, a universal, or another claim beyond the quote). The charge is the premise's own words before its quote (for example "The inference that ..."), read against the words of that quote. Set aside only a clause saying what the premise props ("which props ...") or a sentence naming the objection it serves ("The objection it props is ..."); those are not part of the charge. AGREE with the VOID ruling when the charge goes beyond its quote; DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-COL (a collision line: FORCED, or LINK BROKEN). A link is broken only when the answer's own quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, as the line quotes them; it is not broken because no verse states it, or because of an absence. When the item says the FAILS words are found exactly in the round of the answer, those words are the answering side's own and are read as part of its answer. AGREE when the quoted words show the answer cannot agree with the meaning; DISAGREE when they do carry a meaning the link can agree with, or the line rests on an absence or on a demand for a stating verse.
RULE E-SYN (a sentence of the synthesis saying a side withdrew, conceded, granted, dropped or narrowed something). AGREE when that side's own sentences given you give up that same thing at the same scope; DISAGREE when they do not, or give up less (for example, "no row I cite" is not "no biblical text").
RULE E-HOLD (a collision line graded STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED). STANDS is right only when the answering side's own words, as quoted to you in the line or in this judge's ANSWER CHECK lines, carry a meaning the link can agree with for the meaning pressed. UNDERDETERMINED is right only when the quoted words show that both readings agree with the pressed verse and neither side's words show that the other cannot. BROKEN when the answer's quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, or the answer is only a bare grant or an absence with no fit of its own. A ground that rests on an absence (no verse states it, the text does not narrate it), or on the judge's own reading rather than the debate's words, is not a ground. Each ANSWER CHECK line given you is labelled with whose answer it grades: a MISSES or FAILS on the challenger's answer counts against the challenger's link, never against the defender's, and the reverse. A press labelled UNPROVEN carries no answering burden, so a MISSES on it breaks nothing. For a link-state line ("D5: STANDS"), the quoted answers are that side's ANSWER CHECK lines given you: STANDS is right unless one of them, on a press against this link, is MISSES or FAILS. AGREE when the judge's grade is right; DISAGREE when it is not.
RULE E-KEY (the keystone line). The keystone grade must follow from this judge's own collision lines on that link, given to you: STANDS only when none of them grades the link BROKEN or FORCED and the link was not withdrawn; BROKEN when one of them does. Its ground, where it gives one, must rest on the debate's words, not on the judge's own statement of doctrine. AGREE when the keystone grade follows and its ground rests on the debate's words; DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-PREM (a listed premise, and how each judge ruled it). The judges' own rules, quoted: "A LINK ROUND answer that neither exhibits the premise's layer footing nor concedes counts as CONCEDED." "SELF-SUPPORTED = every listed defender claim is carried by its layer stack -- each [L4] exhibits the [L1]/[L2]/[L3] footing it rests on (at least two prior layers exhibited; a shown chain counts equally)." For a charge in the form ASSUMES: ... -- ROWS GIVE: ...: "the premise is UNEXHIBITED when no quoted row gives the fact it assumes, and it stands when a row the side quoted gives that fact." "UNEXHIBITED also fires ... when a narrowed link keeps words that still assert what its own side gave up." And: "What a link INFERS from its rows is its [L4]: it is graded by the two-layer rule and by the meaning of the verses pressed against it, and never as a missing row (DG-61); an inferred act, such as a begetting or a knowing, is never an ASSUMES." A premise "charged in terms stronger than its quote, is VOID" (RULE E-VOID). For premise N only, decide FIRST the right ruling: COUNTED (UNEXHIBITED or CONCEDED), SPARED, or VOID. The judges' form reads "Itemize the counted links": a premise the judge's line does not name is that judge's SPARED ruling. AGREE when the judge's ruling on premise N (named, or spared by silence) is the right one; DISAGREE when it is not; NO ANSWER only when the judge's line is not in its form. A NARROWED premise (the side drops a claim and keeps the link on a narrower footing, with its [L1] and [L2] or [L3] exhibited) is SPARED: dropping a claim is not conceding the premise, and the dropped claim alone never makes the premise COUNTED. It is UNEXHIBITED only when the kept words still assert the very claim the side dropped; say so by quoting both the dropped claim and the kept words that still assert it.
RULE E-RES (a judge's RESULT line). Its arithmetic is checked in code. Read only its reason sentence: by the judges' Commitment 1 (the record is the only evidence) and Commitment 3 (ruling 405), a reason that rests on an absence (no verse states it, the text does not narrate it) or on the judge's own doctrine rather than the debate's words is not a reason. FOLLOWS when the reason rests on the debate's words; DOES NOT FOLLOW when it does not, quoting the words that show it. AGREE when FOLLOWS; DISAGREE when DOES NOT FOLLOW.
NO ANSWER, for every rule: the judge's line lacks its grade or its ground, or is not in its form. It reports a violation by the judge; it is never your own uncertainty, and you choose AGREE or DISAGREE whenever the line can be read.
Reply with exactly one line per judge id, and nothing else, in this form:
ENFORCER: <judge id> -- AGREE | DISAGREE | NO ANSWER -- RIGHT: MEETS | MISSES | VOID | NOT VOID | BROKEN | STANDS | UNDERDETERMINED | COUNTED | SPARED | FOLLOWS | DOES NOT FOLLOW | TRUE | OVERSTATED -- <one sentence that quotes the words that decide it>

RULE E-ANS (an answer to a pressed verse). Decide FIRST what the right grade is: MEETS only when the answer shows, in its own words, how the verse fits the answering side's case, or why the stated meaning does not follow from what the verse says. MISSES when the answer rests on an absence (it says only that the verse, or the other side, names no, states no, does not name, gives no, or is silent on something) without a fit of its own, or when it does not address the stated meaning. An answer that quotes the verse's own words against the specific claim of the stated meaning (for example, the verse's own stated grounds set against a claim that there were no grounds) shows why the meaning does not follow: it MEETS, even when it closes with a bare assertion such as "It fits the link". Then for each judge's grade: AGREE when it matches the right grade, DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-VOID (a listed premise ruled VOID). A premise is VOID only when its charge says the opponent's quoted words state something they do not state (a negation, a universal, or another claim beyond the quote). The charge is the premise's own words before its quote (for example "The inference that ..."), read against the words of that quote. Set aside only a clause saying what the premise props ("which props ...") or a sentence naming the objection it serves ("The objection it props is ..."); those are not part of the charge. AGREE with the VOID ruling when the charge goes beyond its quote; DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-COL (a collision line: FORCED, or LINK BROKEN). A link is broken only when the answer's own quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, as the line quotes them; it is not broken because no verse states it, or because of an absence. When the item says the FAILS words are found exactly in the round of the answer, those words are the answering side's own and are read as part of its answer. AGREE when the quoted words show the answer cannot agree with the meaning; DISAGREE when they do carry a meaning the link can agree with, or the line rests on an absence or on a demand for a stating verse.
RULE E-SYN (a sentence of the synthesis saying a side withdrew, conceded, granted, dropped or narrowed something). AGREE when that side's own sentences given you give up that same thing at the same scope; DISAGREE when they do not, or give up less (for example, "no row I cite" is not "no biblical text").
RULE E-HOLD (a collision line graded STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED). STANDS is right only when the answering side's own words, as quoted to you in the line or in this judge's ANSWER CHECK lines, carry a meaning the link can agree with for the meaning pressed. UNDERDETERMINED is right only when the quoted words show that both readings agree with the pressed verse and neither side's words show that the other cannot. BROKEN when the answer's quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, or the answer is only a bare grant or an absence with no fit of its own. A ground that rests on an absence (no verse states it, the text does not narrate it), or on the judge's own reading rather than the debate's words, is not a ground. Each ANSWER CHECK line given you is labelled with whose answer it grades: a MISSES or FAILS on the challenger's answer counts against the challenger's link, never against the defender's, and the reverse. A press labelled UNPROVEN carries no answering burden, so a MISSES on it breaks nothing. For a link-state line ("D5: STANDS"), the quoted answers are that side's ANSWER CHECK lines given you: STANDS is right unless one of them, on a press against this link, is MISSES or FAILS. AGREE when the judge's grade is right; DISAGREE when it is not.
RULE E-KEY (the keystone line). The keystone grade must follow from this judge's own collision lines on that link, given to you: STANDS only when none of them grades the link BROKEN or FORCED and the link was not withdrawn; BROKEN when one of them does. Its ground, where it gives one, must rest on the debate's words, not on the judge's own statement of doctrine. AGREE when the keystone grade follows and its ground rests on the debate's words; DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-PREM (a listed premise, and how each judge ruled it). The judges' own rules, quoted: "A LINK ROUND answer that neither exhibits the premise's layer footing nor concedes counts as CONCEDED." "SELF-SUPPORTED = every listed defender claim is carried by its layer stack -- each [L4] exhibits the [L1]/[L2]/[L3] footing it rests on (at least two prior layers exhibited; a shown chain counts equally)." For a charge in the form ASSUMES: ... -- ROWS GIVE: ...: "the premise is UNEXHIBITED when no quoted row gives the fact it assumes, and it stands when a row the side quoted gives that fact." "UNEXHIBITED also fires ... when a narrowed link keeps words that still assert what its own side gave up." And: "What a link INFERS from its rows is its [L4]: it is graded by the two-layer rule and by the meaning of the verses pressed against it, and never as a missing row (DG-61); an inferred act, such as a begetting or a knowing, is never an ASSUMES." A premise "charged in terms stronger than its quote, is VOID" (RULE E-VOID). For premise N only, decide FIRST the right ruling: COUNTED (UNEXHIBITED or CONCEDED), SPARED, or VOID. The judges' form reads "Itemize the counted links": a premise the judge's line does not name is that judge's SPARED ruling. AGREE when the judge's ruling on premise N (named, or spared by silence) is the right one; DISAGREE when it is not; NO ANSWER only when the judge's line is not in its form. A NARROWED premise (the side drops a claim and keeps the link on a narrower footing, with its [L1] and [L2] or [L3] exhibited) is SPARED: dropping a claim is not conceding the premise, and the dropped claim alone never makes the premise COUNTED. It is UNEXHIBITED only when the kept words still assert the very claim the side dropped; say so by quoting both the dropped claim and the kept words that still assert it.
RULE E-RES (a judge's RESULT line). Its arithmetic is checked in code. Read only its reason sentence: by the judges' Commitment 1 (the record is the only evidence) and Commitment 3 (ruling 405), a reason that rests on an absence (no verse states it, the text does not narrate it) or on the judge's own doctrine rather than the debate's words is not a reason. FOLLOWS when the reason rests on the debate's words; DOES NOT FOLLOW when it does not, quoting the words that show it. AGREE when FOLLOWS; DISAGREE when DOES NOT FOLLOW.
NO ANSWER, for every rule: the judge's line lacks its grade or its ground, or is not in its form. It reports a violation by the judge; it is never your own uncertainty, and you choose AGREE or DISAGREE whenever the line can be read.

DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

# Opening: Christ had no biological father

**Term.** By "biological father" I mean a human male who begot the child by natural generation. The KJV text gives Jesus a mother, a legal and supposed father, and a divine origin in the Holy Ghost. It never gives him a human begetter.

## 1. Matthew 1 breaks the "begat" pattern at the exact point of Joseph

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** Matthew 1:2-15 repeats *egennesen* (G1080, "begat"), male begetting male. In verse 16 the pattern changes. Joseph is called *aner* (G435, "husband"), not a begetter. The relative pronoun in "of whom" is *ex hes* (feminine singular, "out of whom"), so the birth is out of Mary alone.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob". This is the unbroken pattern that verse 16 departs from.

**[L4]** The pattern runs "A begat B" fifteen generations running, then stops at Joseph. Joseph is Mary's husband, and the birth is "of whom," the woman. Matthew therefore does not say Joseph begat Jesus. It is the same Matthew who says in 1:18 and 1:20 why not.

## 2. The conception is "of the Holy Ghost"

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** *gennethen* (G1080, "begotten/conceived") is the same verb family used for male begetting in verses 2-16. Here its source is *ek pneumatos hagiou*, "out of the Holy Spirit." That is a source, and the phrase names no human male.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily." Joseph knew he was not the father, so he considered divorce. The angel's correction in 1:20 gives the true source.

**[L4]** The same verb family is used for human begetting in 1:2-16 and for this conception in 1:20. Matthew assigns the source of the conception to the Holy Ghost, and Joseph's intent to put her away shows he was not the source. The text leaves no room for a human begetter.

## 3. "Before they came together" and "knew her not"

**[L1]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."

**[L2]** *ginosko* (G1097, "to know"), used here of marital intimacy, is negated by *ouk* ("not") until the birth. This is also the key word in Mary's question.

**[L3]** Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" The Greek is *andra ou ginosko*: *aner* (G435, "a male man") with *ginosko* negated. Mary says no male has known her.

**[L4]** Matthew 1:18 puts the conception "before they came together," and 1:25 says Joseph "knew her not" until after the birth. Mary herself says she has known no man. Together these two verses exclude a natural begetter before the birth.

## 4. The angel's answer in Luke names the mechanism

**[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

**[L2]** *episkiazo* (G1982, "overshadow") is the verb of divine power. "Therefore" (*dio*, G1352, "for which reason") ties the title "Son of God" to the Holy Ghost's act and to no human generation.

**[L3]** Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph." The woman is *parthenos* (G3933, "virgin") when the angel comes.

**[L4]** Mary's question in 1:34 is about a human male, and the answer in 1:35 supplies a divine source in place of one. That answer explains the birth without a human father.

## 5. Scripture's promised seed is "her seed"

**[L1]** Genesis 3:15: "I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel."

**[L2]** *zera* (H2233, "seed") is attributed to the woman. Scripture elsewhere traces seed through the man.

**[L3]** Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law." The Greek is *genomenon ek gynaikos* (G1096 and G1135), "come to be out of a woman." The source named is a woman and no human male is joined to her.

**[L3]** Hebrews 10:5: "a body hast thou prepared me." The body was prepared (*katartizo*, G2675, "fitted, made ready"), a divine act.

**[L4]** Genesis 3:15 gives the woman a seed, Galatians 4:4 says the Son was "made of a woman," and Hebrews 10:5 says the body was prepared by God. The pattern is consistent: Jesus' human nature comes from a woman by God's act, with no human male named.

## 6. Anticipated objections

**"Thy father" (Luke 2:48) and "the son of Joseph" (John 6:42).**

**[L1]** Luke 2:48: "his mother said unto him, Son, why hast thou thus dealt with us? behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."

**[L3]** Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" Jesus immediately corrects whose father he means.

**[L1]** Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."

**[L2]** *enomizeto* (G3543, "was supposed, was reckoned") marks a belief, an opinion held by people. It does not state a fact.

**[L1]** John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" The speakers are the Jews murmuring. Their phrase reports what they "know"; the text itself says "as was supposed."

**[L4]** Luke 3:23 labels the Joseph relation "supposed," and Luke 2:49 reassigns the title "Father." Joseph's role is legal and household headship, not begetting.

**"Seed of David / fruit of his loins" (Romans 1:3; Acts 2:30).**

**[L1]** Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh."

**[L1]** Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne."

**[L2]** *ek spermatos* (G4690, "out of the seed") speaks of descent, and descent can run through the mother. Romans 1:3 uses *genomenon* (G1096, "made, come to be"), the same word as in Galatians 4:4 for "made of a woman."

**[L3]** Luke 3:31: "which was the son of Nathan, which was the son of David." Luke's genealogy runs through Nathan, a different son of David from the line in Matthew 1:6-7, where Solomon's line runs to Joseph.

**[L4]** Romans 1:3 and Galatians 4:4 use the same verb *genomenon*. Davidic descent "according to the flesh" is therefore carried by the woman, so a human male begetter is not required to supply it.

## DECLARED CHAIN -- the links your case stands on:

1. Matthew's genealogy stops saying "begat" at Joseph and shifts to "of whom was born Jesus" (feminine *ex hes*, "out of whom"): [L1] Matthew 1:16 "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus"; [L2] *egennesen* (begat) versus *ex hes* (out of her); [L3] Matthew 1:2 "Abraham begat Isaac".
2. The conception is "of the Holy Ghost," with Joseph excluded as source: [L1] Matthew 1:20 "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost"; [L2] *ek pneumatos hagiou* (out of the Holy Spirit); [L3] Matthew 1:19 Joseph "was minded to put her away privily."
3. Mary had known no man, and Joseph "knew her not" until the birth: [L1] Matthew 1:25 "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son"; [L2] *ginosko* (to know) and *andra* (man, male); [L3] Luke 1:34 "seeing I know not a man."
4. The angel names the mechanism as the Holy Ghost's power: [L1] Luke 1:35 "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee"; [L2] *episkiazo* (overshadow) and *dio* (therefore); [L3] Luke 1:27 "a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph."
5. The "father" and "son of Joseph" language is supposed or legal, and the "seed of David" descent runs through the woman: [L1] Luke 3:23 "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph"; [L2] *enomizeto* (was supposed) and *genomenon* (made, come to be); [L3] Luke 2:49 "my Father's business" and Galatians 4:4 "made of a woman."
6. Christ had no biological human father: [L1] Matthew 1:18 "found with child of the Holy Ghost"; [L2] *ek pneumatos hagiou* (out of the Holy Spirit) as the stated source; [L3] Luke 1:35 "that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
