# Round 2: Defender's answer

I answer each press by its own rows, then the question on Hebrews 7:14. I release some weight where the challenger is right.

## What I release (discipline)

- **[L1]** Galatians 4:4: "made of a woman." **[L3]** Job 14:1: "Man [that is] born of a woman." **[L4]** Job 14:1 and Matthew 11:11 apply "of a woman" to men who had fathers, so Galatians 4:4 does not carry the exclusion alone. I withdraw it as load-bearing. It is consistent with my case and does not prove it.
- **[L3]** Genesis 3:15 "her seed" is supporting only, for the same reason (Genesis 4:25).
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:19 carries intent and grounds, not a verb of knowing. My opening sentence "Joseph knew he was not the father" overstated. I restate it below as an inference from three rows.

## Against the challenge on D1: the verb stops at Joseph

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus."

**[L2]** *gennaō* (G1080, "to procreate, properly of the father, by extension of the mother") stands in the active, "begat," through verses 2-16 with a man as subject. At verse 16 it stands in the passive, "was born," with the child as subject and the woman as source (*ex hēs*, "out of whom").

**[L3]** Matthew 1:3: "Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar." Matthew 1:6: "David the king begat Solomon of her [that had been the wife] of Urias."

**[L4]** The challenger is right that "of [a woman]" does not remove a father in 1:3, 1:5 and 1:6. In each of those verses a man is the subject of the active "begat" and the woman is added. In 1:16 Matthew keeps the active verb for Jacob and Joseph, then changes to the passive for Jesus, so no man is the subject of a begetting for him. The pattern that keeps the father when a woman is named in 1:3, 1:5 and 1:6 is the pattern 1:16 leaves.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise." This is Matthew's own signal that the manner of this birth differs from the preceding "begat" lines. The same passive verb of 1:16 returns in 1:20 with a named source.

## Against the challenge on D2: "of the Holy Ghost"

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"

**[L2]** The sheet's gloss for *gennaō* is "properly, of the father," with "figuratively, to regenerate" listed separately. In 1:20 the object is "that which is begotten *in her*," in the womb. **[L1]** Matthew 1:18 puts the same fact as "found with child of the Holy Ghost"; **[L2]** *gastēr* (G1064, "womb") belongs to the physical state of being with child.

**[L3]** The challenger's 1 John 5:1 and John 1:13 are the figurative "regenerate" sense: believers "born... of God." **[L1]** John 1:13 says that birth is "not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God." **[L4]** John 1:13 sets "of God" against "of man" as the begetting source. It never places a figurative birth in a womb. In Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 the thing is "in her" and its source is "of the Holy Ghost," and no man is named as source. The challenger's reading of 1:20 as spiritual origin does not meet "found with child" (1:18).

**Joseph's knowledge (restated as inference).**

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:19: "Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
- **[L2]** *paradeigmatizō* (G3856, "to expose to infamy") and *láthra* (G2977, "secretly") name a shame to be hidden. *dikaios* (G1342, "just, equitable") is why he would not take her as she was.
- **[L3]** Deuteronomy 22:23-24, the challenger's own rows: a betrothed damsel with a man is judged as "his neighbour's wife" humbled, and stoning follows.
- **[L4]** A husband who had known his wife and was the father would have no infamy to hide and no reason to put her away. The just man's plan answers a pregnancy he took to be from another. Matthew 1:20 then answers his fear ("fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife") by naming the source ("of the Holy Ghost"). A reason that removes the fear of a wrong must name a source other than a wrongdoer. This is the force of "for," and it works as a source notice by function.

## Against the challenge on D3: Luke 1:34 and Matthew 1:18-25

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" **[L3]** Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb."

**[L4]** The challenger is right that the verb is present (*ginōskō*, G1097, "to know"). "This" in 1:34 is the conception of 1:31, and "how" asks its means. If the means were Joseph after the wedding, the question would have an obvious answer, and the angel gives a different one: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee" (Luke 1:35). **[L1]** Luke 1:37: "For with God nothing shall be impossible." That sentence has no work to do if a husband is to be the means. **[L3]** Luke 1:36 gives the sign, Elisabeth "who was called barren."

**[L1]** Matthew 1:23: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son." **[L2]** *parthenos* (G3933, "virgin") is the word Matthew gives for the one who "shall be with child." **[L3]** Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son," given as "a sign" in the same verse. **[L4]** A sign from the Lord that is an ordinary conception by a husband is no sign. The challenger has not answered Matthew 1:23.

**The order in Matthew 1:18-25.**

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child." **[L1]** Matthew 1:24: "took unto him his wife." **[L1]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
- **[L2]** The negative with *ginōskō* in 1:25 is the verse's own statement of knowing and not knowing. "Came together" (*synerchomai*, G4905, "to come together") is the challenger's gloss for dwelling in one house, but 1:25 tells what "knew" means here.
- **[L4]** The challenger puts Joseph's knowing before the taking, within the espousal. He rests it on Deuteronomy 22:24 ("neighbour's wife"), which gives status and says nothing of intimacy. His other row is Genesis 4:1, "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived," which is another couple. For Adam the text states the knowing. For Joseph and Mary it states "knew her not" (1:25), and the pregnancy stands before the angel and before the taking (1:18, 1:24). A knowing before the taking would be the cause of the "found with child" that 1:19 treats as shame and 1:20 as "of the Holy Ghost." Matthew 1:25 then protects the account: Joseph took her and still did not know her till the birth.

## Against the challenge on D4: Luke 1:35

**[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

**[L2]** *eperchomai* (G1904, "to come upon") and *episkiazō* (G1982, "to overshadow") are as the challenger says: presence and power. **[L3]** Acts 1:8, Luke 9:34, Acts 5:15.

**[L4]** I grant that those verbs, alone, are not begetting. They are not alone here. Three things fix their sense in Luke 1:35:

1. They answer the question "How shall this be?" (1:34), which is about a conception.
2. They are followed by *dio* (G1352, "therefore"), which ties the birth of "that holy thing... of thee" to the Holy Ghost's coming. The "therefore" falls inside the verse on the clauses it follows.
3. In Acts 1:8 and Luke 9:34 the persons already exist. In Luke 1:35 the "therefore" attaches to a birth that has no other source named.

**[L3]** The challenger sends "therefore" back to 1:32 and the covenant title of 2 Samuel 7:14 and 1 Chronicles 28:6. **[L1]** Solomon is called "my son" with a named father in the same verse (1 Chronicles 28:6). **[L4]** In Luke 1:35 the angel gives the reason for the title as the Holy Ghost's act on Mary, and no man is named. The covenant parallel to Solomon explains the title. It does not explain why this answer to "how" names no man.

**[L3]** Psalm 2:7, Acts 13:33 and Romans 1:4 locate "begotten" at the raising. I do not rest on Psalm 2:7. Matthew 1:20 states a begetting in the womb, and Romans 1:4 says "declared [to be] the Son of God with power... by the resurrection," which declares a Sonship and does not locate the conception.

## Against the challenge on D5: seed, loins and Joseph's house

**[L1]** Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh." **[L2]** *sperma* (G4690, "seed") in the sheet's gloss is "seed (including the male 'sperm'); by implication, offspring." **[L3]** Matthew 1:6: "David the king begat Solomon of her [that had been the wife] of Urias."

**[L4]** The word covers offspring across generations. David's "seed" and "loins" (Acts 2:30, *osphys*, G3751, "loins") reach a descendant about a thousand years on. **[L3]** Hebrews 7:5 uses "loins of Abraham" for all who "come out of" him, and those descendants had mothers of other houses. "Loins" names descent from David and does not require that the last link be a father.

**Mary's descent from David is not left to Luke 1:27.** I concede the KJV's clause "of the house of David" in Luke 1:27 can attach to Joseph, and I do not rest on it.

- **[L1]** Luke 1:32, said to Mary: "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David." **[L1]** Luke 1:35: "that holy thing which shall be born of thee." **[L1]** Luke 3:31: "which was [the son] of Nathan, which was [the son] of David." **[L2]** *gennaō* (G1080) is the word of "born" in Matthew 1:16.
- **[L3]** Luke 3:23: "the son of Joseph, which was [the son] of Heli." **[L3]** Matthew 1:16: "Jacob begat Joseph."
- **[L4]** The KJV prints "[the son]" in brackets at Luke 3:23, supplied words. Matthew gives Joseph's begetter as Jacob, Luke names Heli. The challenger says Luke's line "runs to Nathan through Joseph's name," which sets two begetters over one man. If Joseph's line is Jacob's in Matthew, then Luke's second line, in which the child's descent from David comes through the child born "of thee," is Mary's side (Heli). The two lists name two houses by two ancestors, and "[the son]" in Luke 3:23 is added.

**The line through Solomon is cut for a male begetter.**

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:11: "Josias begat Jechonias." **[L1]** Matthew 1:12: "Jechonias begat Salathiel." **[L1]** Matthew 1:16 brings the line to Joseph.
- **[L3]** Jeremiah 22:24: "Coniah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah." 1 Chronicles 3:16: "Jeconiah his son." Jeremiah 22:30: "no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David."
- **[L4]** Luke 1:32 promises this child the throne of David. A son begotten by Joseph, whose line passes through Jechonias (Matthew 1:11-12, 1:16), is "of his seed," and Jeremiah 22:30 says no man of that seed shall sit on David's throne. A child born "of thee" (Luke 1:35) and not begotten by Joseph is outside that seed, while Joseph's naming of him (Matthew 1:21, "thou shalt call his name JESUS"; 1:25) gives the legal side. This chain stands on two verses of Matthew, one of Chronicles and two of Jeremiah, and no row in the record answers it.

**"As was supposed" and "thy father."**

- **[L1]** Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph." **[L2]** *nomizō* (G3543, "to deem, to think by custom") is rendered "supposed" by the KJV. **[L3]** Luke 2:44: "supposing him to have been in the company," and he was not. Acts 14:19: "supposing he had been dead," and he was not. **[L4]** In the same Gospel, a few verses before Luke 2:48, the KJV uses this word of a supposition that proved false. Acts 16:13 ("wont to be made") is a different sense of the same root, and the challenger offers no row to make Luke 3:23 that one. A narrator does not put "as was supposed" in parentheses at an ordinary father and son.
- **[L1]** Luke 2:48: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." **[L1]** Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" **[L3]** Luke 2:50: "And they understood not the saying which he spake unto them." **[L4]** Mary speaks of "thy father," and the reply gives the title to another Father. The two do not stand together as in 1 Chronicles 28:6, where the same speaker names both. Here the reply corrects the assumption.
- **[L1]** John 6:42: "whose father and mother we know? how is it then that he saith, I came down from heaven?" **[L3]** Luke 2:27 "the parents," Luke 2:33 "Joseph and his mother." **[L4]** Luke's own narration says "the parents" and "Joseph and his mother." The phrase "his father" is in the mouths of the people and of Mary speaking in worry.

## Against D6: the question on Hebrews 7:14

**[L1]** Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda."

**[L2]** *anatellō* (G393, "to arise, to spring up") says he arose out of Juda. It names the tribe and says nothing of which parent carries it.

**[L4]** How is it "evident"? By the public record. **[L1]** Matthew 1:2: "Jacob begat Judas and his brethren." **[L1]** Luke 3:31 puts him in David's line by Nathan. **[L4]** Matthew 1:16 legally reckons him to Joseph, and Luke 1:32-35 and Luke 3:31 give the born-of-her line. Both are open to Judah.

**[L3]** Numbers 1:2 and 1:18 are a census of "every male by their polls," a muster list of men able to go to war. They are not a rule that a tribe passes only by a father. **[L3]** Numbers 27:8: "If a man die, and have no son, then ye shall cause his inheritance to pass unto his daughter." **[L3]** Numbers 36:8 keeps that daughter inside the "tribe of her father." **[L3]** Ezra 2:61 shows a man "called after their name," his wife's family. **[L4]** The law the challenger cites reckons through the father's house in the muster and lets house and name pass through a daughter in the cases it names. Ezra 2:62 is the penalty for not finding "their register," not a rule against the mother's line.

**[L1]** Hebrews 2:17: "in all things it behoved him to be made like unto [his] brethren." **[L3]** Hebrews 4:15: "was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin." **[L4]** The text itself limits "in all things." A likeness that already stops at sin cannot be pressed to mean he shares the manner of generation. **[L1]** Hebrews 2:14 says he "took part of the same" flesh and blood, and 2:16 says he took "the seed of Abraham." Both name what he took, not who begot him. **[L1]** Hebrews 10:5: "a body hast thou prepared me." **[L3]** Genesis 4:1 has "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived" before "I have gotten a man from the LORD." The knowing is stated there. In Hebrews 10:5, as in Matthew 1:25, it is not.

## Declared chain after Round 2

1. Matthew 1:16 keeps the active "begat" for Jacob and Joseph and turns to the passive for Jesus, "of whom was born": [L1] Matthew 1:16; [L2] *gennaō* (G1080, to procreate, of the father) active then passive; [L3] Matthew 1:3, 1:6.
2. The thing "begotten in her" is "of the Holy Ghost," which fits no man's place: [L1] Matthew 1:20; [L2] *gastēr* (G1064, womb) in the "with child" of 1:18; [L3] John 1:13.
3. Joseph's plan to put her away and Matthew 1:25 give no room for his knowing her before the birth: [L1] Matthew 1:19, 1:25; [L2] *paradeigmatizō* (G3856, expose to infamy) and *ginōskō* (G1097, to know); [L3] Deuteronomy 22:24.
4. The angel's answer to "how" names the Holy Ghost, with a sign of a virgin: [L1] Luke 1:35; [L2] *dio* (G1352, therefore); [L3] Matthew 1:23, Isaiah 7:14.
5. "Son of Joseph" is supposed and legal, and David's throne reaches the child by Mary's line past the cut in Jechonias's seed: [L1] Luke 3:23; [L2] *nomizō* (G3543, to suppose); [L3] Luke 2:44, Jeremiah 22:30.
6. Christ had no biological human father: [L1] Matthew 1:18; [L2] *ek* with the Holy Ghost as source; [L3] Luke 1:35.

## LINK ROUND

**LINK 1: SUPPORTED**

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
- **[L2]** *gennaō* (G1080, "to procreate, properly of the father") is the verb in every "begat" of the line. At Matthew 1:16 the "of whom" is the feminine singular relative *hēs* ("of whom," pointing to Mary alone). It is not the masculine, which would point back to Joseph.
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac." Matthew 1:3: "Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar." Matthew 1:5: "Booz begat Obed of Ruth."
- **[L4]** Footing: the L1 verse, the L2 feminine "of whom," and the L3 pattern.
  1. In Matthew 1:2-16 every father is the subject of "begat."
  2. At the one place where Jesus comes into the line, the subject is not a man. The relative turns to Mary alone.
  3. So the line names Joseph "the husband of Mary" and stops short of "Joseph begat Jesus."

*Presses answered*
- Matthew 1:3, "Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar," and Matthew 1:5, "Salmon begat Booz of Rachab." In both the man is the subject of "begat" beside the woman. That is the contrast. Where a father begets, the text writes him as subject. At 1:16 it does not.
- Matthew 11:11, "Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist." I grant that a bare passive proves no absence. The link rests on the contrast of subjects. Luke 1:13 also puts the father in the row: "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son." Matthew 1:21 reads "she shall bring forth a son," with no "thee."
- Matthew 1:19, "Then Joseph her husband," and Matthew 1:20, "Mary thy wife." *anēr* (G435, "a man, husband") gives Joseph the title of husband. Matthew 1:16 and 1:19 give that title and no row writes "father."

**LINK 2: SUPPORTED**

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"
- **[L2]** *gennaō* (G1080, "to procreate"), the margin's "begotten," is the verb Matthew gave the fathers in 1:2-16. Here its source is "the Holy Ghost."
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:18: "she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." Luke 1:35: "that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- **[L4]** Footing: L1, L2, L3. The thing "in her" has as its source the Holy Ghost, in the verb that elsewhere in the chapter has a man as source. Of the thing conceived, no row names a man.

*Presses answered*
- 1 John 5:1, "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God," and John 1:13, "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God." John 1:13 itself sets "of God" against "the will of man." It is said of believers after faith. Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 say "of the Holy Ghost" of "that which is conceived in her," at the conception and before the birth.
- John 3:6, "that which is born of the Spirit is spirit." It names a birth of spirit in believers. It does not read as the conception of a child "found with child" (Matthew 1:18).
- Romans 1:3, "made of the seed of David according to the flesh." *sperma* (G4690, "seed, offspring") is descent from David. Hebrews 2:16 uses the same word: "he took on [him] the seed of Abraham." Romans 1:3 names David's seed and does not name Joseph as begetter. Hebrews 10:5 says of the body: "a body hast thou prepared me."
- 1 Chronicles 28:6, "I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father," and 2 Samuel 7:14, "I will be his father, and he shall be my son." In both the sonship rests on God's choice of one already born, and the human father is called "thy son's" father in the verse. Luke 1:35 gives a cause at the conception, "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee... therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee." The angel does not say "thy son" to Joseph (Matthew 1:21).

**LINK 3: SUPPORTED**

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- **[L2]** *boulomai* (G1014, "to be minded") and *apolyō* (G630, "to put away, divorce") stand in Matthew 1:19. *paradeigmatizō* (G3856, "to expose to infamy") names what he would not do.
- **[L3]** Deuteronomy 24:1: "because he hath found some uncleanness in her... let him write her a bill of divorcement." Deuteronomy 22:23: "a man find her in the city, and lie with her." Matthew 1:25: "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
- **[L4]** Footing: L1, L2, L3.
  1. Matthew 1:18 puts the finding "before they came together."
  2. Matthew 1:25 puts the not-knowing from the taking to the birth.
  3. No row leaves a time before the birth when they came together. So the pregnancy found is not one he caused.
  4. Deuteronomy 24:1 gives the ground for divorce as "uncleanness found," not a wife carrying her husband's child.
  5. The angel's "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife" (Matthew 1:20) answers a fear about taking her. A father would have no such fear.

*Presses answered*
- Matthew 1:19 states two grounds, justice and unwillingness to expose. Both fit mine. *dikaios* (G1342, "just, equitable") is why he would not take a wife found with child before they came together, and unwillingness to expose is why he would do it privily.
- Deuteronomy 22:24, "his neighbour's wife," and Matthew 1:24, "took unto him his wife." I grant that the betrothed was a wife in law. Deuteronomy 22:23 treats lying with her as a separate act after betrothal, and Deuteronomy 20:7 treats taking as a further step after betrothal. Betrothed as wife does not say "came together."
- Genesis 4:1, "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived." *yada* (H3045, "to know, lie with") there joins the knowing to the conception. Matthew 1:18 and 1:25 deny the knowing before the birth. Matthew 1:20 gives the Holy Ghost as source.
- Luke 1:31, "thou shalt conceive in thy womb," is future. Luke 1:34, "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" is asked of that future conception, and Luke 1:35 answers with the Holy Ghost in place of a man.

**LINK 4: SUPPORTED**

- **[L1]** Isaiah 7:14: "Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."
- **[L2]** *almah* (H5959, the word behind the KJV's "virgin") is the word the KJV prints "virgin" here. The KJV prints the Greek in Matthew 1:23, "a virgin shall be with child," with *parthenos* (G3933, "virgin"), and Matthew 1:25 says she was not known till the birth.
- **[L3]** Isaiah 8:3: "Call his name Mahershalalhashbaz." Isaiah 7:14: "shall call his name Immanuel." Matthew 1:22: "Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled."
- **[L4]** Footing: L1, L2, L3. Matthew states the sign as fulfilled in a woman found with child "before they came together" (Matthew 1:18). A "sign" that falls in the very condition Matthew states is not an ordinary conception by a husband.

*Presses answered*
- Isaiah 8:3, "And I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son." That child is told "Call his name Mahershalalhashbaz," and the sign child's name in Isaiah 7:14 is Immanuel. Isaiah 8:8, "O Immanuel," addresses the land, not that son. So the two are not shown to be one child.
- Isaiah 7:16, "before the child shall know to refuse the evil." I take it as the nearer sign to Ahaz. Matthew 1:22-23 applies the verse to the conception of Jesus, and Matthew states the fulfilment.
- Luke 1:36 and Luke 1:15, "he shall be filled with the Holy Ghost, even from his mother's womb." Elisabeth's sign is that she "was called barren." Luke 1:13 says "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son," with "thee." Luke 1:35 says "born of thee," and Matthew 1:21 says "she shall bring forth a son," with no "thee." John is *filled* in the womb. Jesus is *begotten* of the Holy Ghost (Matthew 1:20, the margin). The two verbs differ.
- Acts 1:8, "after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you," and Luke 9:34, "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them." In both the persons already exist. In Luke 1:35 the thing "which shall be born of thee" does not yet exist.
- Luke 1:32 and Luke 1:35 together: "therefore also" (*dio kai*) in 1:35 stands in the same verse as the two clauses before it, "come upon thee... overshadow thee," and gives their result.

**LINK 5: NARROWED TO:** (A) a child not begotten by Joseph is not of Coniah's seed by the flesh; (B) his flesh is of David's seed through Mary. I drop the house-by-Heli reading as a stated fact. No row names Mary's father.

- **[L1]** Jeremiah 22:30: "no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David, and ruling any more in Judah."
- **[L3] for A:** Matthew 1:12: "Jechonias begat Salathiel." Matthew 1:16: "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary." Luke 1:32: "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David." Matthew 1:20: "of the Holy Ghost."
- **[L4] for A:** Matthew 1:12 begins the line after Jechonias and 1:16 ends it at Joseph. A son begotten by Joseph would be "of his seed." Luke 1:32 gives Jesus the throne, so by Jeremiah 22:30 he cannot be of that seed by the flesh.
- **[L1] for B:** Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh." Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ."
- **[L2] for B:** *osphys* (G3751, "loins") at Acts 2:30 and *sperma* (G4690, "seed") at Romans 1:3 name the flesh as David's.
- **[L3] for B:** Luke 1:35: "which shall be born of thee." Matthew 1:21: "she shall bring forth a son."
- **[L4] for B:** If Joseph did not beget him, the flesh from David comes through the one "of whom" he was born. That makes it through Mary.

*Presses answered*
- Matthew 1:12 and 1 Chronicles 3:17, "Assir, Salathiel his son." I grant that Coniah has sons. Jeremiah 22:30 speaks of no man of his seed "sitting upon the throne," and A rests on that.
- Haggai 2:23, "will make thee as a signet: for I have chosen thee." The row says signet and chosen. It does not say sitting on the throne.
- Jeremiah 18:8, "If that nation, against whom I have pronounced, turn from their evil, I will repent of the evil." It is conditioned on the nation's turning, and Jeremiah 18:7 names a nation. No row says Coniah's seed turned.
- Luke 3:27, "which was [the son] of Zorobabel, which was [the son] of Salathiel, which was [the son] of Neri." Neri here is the father, where Matthew 1:12 has Jechonias. I make no claim that these are the same men.
- Luke 2:4 and Luke 1:27 give Joseph the house of David, and I accept that. Luke 1:36 and Luke 1:5 name Mary's kin only as Elisabeth, "of the daughters of Aaron." They do not name Mary's own line. B does not rest on a named father of Mary.
- Acts 2:30 and Psalms 132:11, "Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne." Both name David's body or loins, not Joseph's.

**LINK 6: NARROWED TO:** the law lets inheritance and the house's name pass through a daughter (Numbers 27:8; Numbers 36:8; Ezra 2:61), and Hebrews 7:14 states Judah as the origin without naming a father. I concede that the muster is by the fathers' house.

- **[L1]** Numbers 27:8: "ye shall cause his inheritance to pass unto his daughter." Ezra 2:61: "took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called after their name."
- **[L3]** Numbers 36:8: "shall be wife unto one of the family of the tribe of her father."
- **[L4]** Footing: L1 and L3. The law carries inheritance through a daughter in the cases it names, and Ezra 2:61 gives a priest the name of his wife's house. So the muster by the fathers' house (Numbers 1:2; 1:18) does not shut the daughter out.

*Presses answered*
- Hebrews 7:14, "evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda." The row states the tribe and names no father.
- Numbers 1:2 and 1:18, "by the house of their fathers." Granted, the muster is by the fathers' house.
- Ezra 2:59 and Ezra 2:62, "therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood." The row's reason is that "they were not found" in the register (Ezra 2:62). It is not a ruling on a name through a wife.
- Hebrews 2:14, "he also himself likewise took part of the same." The likeness is in "flesh and blood" (*haima*, G129, "blood"; *sarx*, G4561, "flesh"), which are the nature. "Took part" is his own act. Hebrews 10:5 says "a body hast thou prepared me."
- Hebrews 2:17, "in all things it behoved him to be made like unto [his] brethren," and Hebrews 4:15, "yet without sin." The limit named is sin. The verses state likeness of nature and condition. They do not state sameness of how he came to be.
- Luke 2:48, "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." Luke 3:23 marks the same sense, "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph." Luke 2:49 answers "thy father" with "my Father's business," and Luke 2:50 adds "And they understood not the saying which he spake unto them."

# Challenge: the record names the father, and the seed came out of a man's loins

The defender's chain rests on three readings. It reads one passive verb (Matthew 1:16) as a statement of absence. It reads a present-tense state (Luke 1:34) as a permanent one. It reads "of the Holy Ghost" as a begetting, which the same Greek construction never means when it is said of believers. Each is answered below by its own row, link by link, ending at the keystone D6.

---

## Against D1: "of whom" names the mother, as it does four times earlier in the same genealogy

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** "Of whom" is *ex hēs*: *ek* (G1537, "out of") with the feminine pronoun. Matthew uses the same *ek* with a woman's name inside the "begat" pattern itself, with the father as the subject of the verb.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:3: "And Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar." Matthew 1:5: "And Salmon begat Booz of Rachab; and Booz begat Obed of Ruth."

**[L4]** In 1:3 and 1:5, "of [a woman]" (*ek* with a feminine name) stands in the same sentence as a man's *egennēsen*. So *ek* with a mother names the mother; it does not remove the father. Verse 16 changes the subject of its verb to the child: "was born," passive. That says what happened to the child. It does not narrate who begat him. The defender's L4, "Matthew therefore does not say Joseph begat Jesus," turns a verb that does not narrate the begetting into a statement that there was none. It also overlooks that the same verse calls Joseph "the husband (*anēr*, G435) of Mary." That is the word of Matthew 1:19, "Joseph her husband," and of Deuteronomy 22:23, a virgin "betrothed unto an husband."

## Against D2: Matthew 1:20 names Joseph in the same row, and "of God" is said of believers

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"

**[L2]** The margin's verb is *gennaō* (G1080, "to procreate"). The same verb, with "of God," is said of believers.

**[L3]** 1 John 5:1: "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God: and every one that loveth him that begat loveth him also that is begotten of him. [is born: Gr. has been born]" John 1:13: "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God." John 3:6: "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit."

**[L3]** When the text means flesh, it adds the flesh-marker. Romans 1:3: "which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh" (*ek spermatos Dauid kata sarka*; *sperma*, G4690, "seed"; *sarx*, "flesh").

**[L4]** "Begotten ... of God" at 1 John 5:1 and John 1:13 is a spiritual origin for men who each had a human father. Matthew 1:20 uses the same verb with "of the Holy Ghost" and carries no "according to the flesh." Where the flesh is meant, Romans 1:3 says "according to the flesh" and names David's seed. The row that says "of the Holy Ghost" also names "Joseph, thou son of David" and "Mary thy wife," and both are to be held together. The angel's "for" (*gar*) grounds the command "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife." It is the reason to take her, not a paternity notice.

**Matthew 1:19 at the word.** The verse reads: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily." **[L2]** "Was minded" is *eboulēthē*, an intent. **[L1]** Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

**[L2]** *andra ou ginōskō* is present active indicative: her state at the moment she spoke.

**[L3]** Luke 1:31, three verses earlier: "And, behold, thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son." Here "shalt conceive" is future (*syllēmpsē*). Luke 1:27 likewise describes her when the angel came: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David."

**[L4]** Luke 1:27 and 1:34 describe Mary on the day of the announcement. Luke 1:31 puts the conception after that day. So the defender's L4, "Mary says no male has known her," fits the time before the conception. It does not fit the conception itself.

**Matthew 1:18 and 1:25, quoted as written and read in their order.**
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:24: "Then Joseph ... took unto him his wife."
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."

**[L4]** Matthew sets the order himself:
1. The finding comes before the taking (1:18).
2. The taking follows: "took unto him his wife" (1:24).

**[L1]** 2 Samuel 7:12: "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels." Psalm 132:11: "Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne. [body: Heb. belly]" Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne."

**[L2]** "Loins" at Acts 2:30 is *osphys* (G3751). It is the word of Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father." **[L3]** It is also the word of Hebrews 7:5: "though they come out of the loins of Abraham."

**"Made of a woman" is said of men whose fathers are named.**

**LINK 1: SUPPORTED** (Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal)

- **[L1]** 2 Samuel 7:12: "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels." Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne." The promised seed comes out of a man's body.
- **[L2]** *sperma* (G4690, "something sown, i.e. seed (including the male 'sperm'); by implication, offspring") in Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh." *yada* (H3045, "to know... lie by man") in Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the LORD. [Cain: that is, Gotten, or, Acquired]"
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband." Here *anēr* (G435) means "husband." Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife." Here *gynē* (G1135) means "specially, a wife." Deuteronomy 22:24 calls a betrothed damsel "his neighbour's wife." Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."
- **[L4]** The chain:
  1. The seed is required out of a man's bowels and loins, "according to the flesh" (2 Samuel 7:12; Acts 2:30; Romans 1:3, *sperma*).
  2. The canon's stated means of begetting is a husband knowing his wife (Genesis 4:1, *yada*).
  3. The one man the text names beside Mary is "Joseph her husband," and she is "Mary thy wife" from the espousal (Matthew 1:19-20; Deuteronomy 22:24).
  4. Matthew 1:25 sets "till" on the abstinence and bounds it to the pregnancy.
  5. So Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is "of the seed of David according to the flesh."

*Presses answered*
- **Matthew 1:18**, "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." The verse dates the finding. Matthew sets what "came together" means by what follows: Matthew 1:24, "took unto him his wife." There *paralambanō* (G3880) means "to receive near, i.e. associate with oneself." That is her coming into his house. The law names the same step in Deuteronomy 20:7: "hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her." So "before they came together" is before the taking. The espousal, in which she is already "Mary thy wife" (Matthew 1:20), stands before that taking. It fits the link.
- **Matthew 1:25**, "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." Its span follows Matthew 1:24, "took unto him his wife." The not-knowing covers the house-time of the pregnancy, from the taking to the birth. The espousal-time stands before the taking (Deuteronomy 20:7). The "till" (Matthew 1:25) bounds the abstinence to the pregnancy. It fits the link.
- **Deuteronomy 22:23**, "If a damsel [that is] a virgin be betrothed unto an husband, and a man find her in the city, and lie with her." The act the law judges is another man's: "a man find her." Deuteronomy 22:24 names his guilt, "he hath humbled his neighbour's wife." The betrothed husband is the one she is "betrothed unto." His knowing of his own wife is the pattern of Genesis 4:1, "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived." The law's word for her is *ishshah* (H802, "wife"). It fits the link.
- **Luke 1:34**, "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" The verb *ginōskō* (G1097, "know") stands in the present indicative. It gives her state when the angel spoke. Luke 1:31 places the conception after that word: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb." There *syllambanō* (G4815, "to conceive") is future. A present state on the day of the word sits before a future conception. The espousal in which the conception falls is the one Luke 1:27 names: "a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David." It fits the link.

**LINK 2: SUPPORTED** (Luke 1:37 is a sign drawn from a conception with a named father)

- **[L1]** Luke 1:36: "And, behold, thy cousin Elisabeth, she hath also conceived a son in her old age: and this is the sixth month with her, who was called barren." Luke 1:37: "For with God nothing shall be impossible."
- **[L2]** *syllambanō* (G4815, "to conceive") is the verb of Elisabeth's conception in Luke 1:36. It is the same verb given to Mary in Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb." The angel's "also" sets the two conceptions side by side in one verb.
- **[L3]** Luke 1:13: "Fear not, Zacharias: for thy prayer is heard; and thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John."
- **[L4]** The chain:
  1. The angel gives Mary, as his "For," the conception of Elisabeth (Luke 1:36-37).
  2. Elisabeth's conception has a named father in the row, "shall bear thee a son" (Luke 1:13).
  3. So the sign of Luke 1:37 is drawn from a conception with a named father.

*Presses answered*
- **Luke 1:13**, "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son." The "thee" is the named father my premise states. The angel speaks "thee" to the man he addresses. In Matthew the angel addresses Joseph with the same father's command: Matthew 1:21, "And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins. [JESUS: that is, Saviour, Heb]." Zacharias receives "thou shalt call his name John" (Luke 1:13). Joseph receives "thou shalt call his name JESUS" (Matthew 1:21), and does it: "he called his name JESUS" (Matthew 1:25). The naming command falls to the husband in both rows. It fits the link.
- **Luke 1:15**, "he shall be filled with the Holy Ghost, even from his mother's womb." The sign Luke 1:36 gives is the conception, *syllambanō*, which is not the filling. Luke 1:15 shows the Holy Ghost upon a child whose father is named in Luke 1:13. So the Holy Ghost's work and a named father stand together in one child. It fits the link.
- **Luke 1:36**, "who was called barren." What God overcame in Elisabeth was barrenness, in a conception with her husband, "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son" (Luke 1:13). The angel sets Mary's conception beside it with "also" (Luke 1:36, *syllambanō*), and "nothing shall be impossible" covers both. It fits the link.

- **Isaiah 8:8**, "the stretching out of his wings shall fill the breadth of thy land, O Immanuel. [stretching...: Heb. fulness of the breadth of thy land shall be the stretchings out of his wings]." The verse addresses a person who owns the land, "thy land, O Immanuel." The overflowing of Judah by Assyria in Isaiah 8:7-8 is the event Isaiah 8:4 times by the child's "My father, and my mother." Immanuel recurs in Isaiah's own day, inside the same Assyrian sign. It fits the link.
- **Matthew 1:23**, "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us. [they...: or, his name shall be called]." Matthew sets the fulfilment in a house with a named husband. Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]." Matthew 1:25: "he called his name JESUS," the husband's act. The word *parthenos* (G3933) is Matthew's word in the received Greek. # ROUND 4: CHALLENGER'S CLOSE

**Did Christ have a biological father?** The scripture, read precept upon precept (Isaiah 28:10), answers yes. It names Joseph as the man through whom the promised seed of David came "according to the flesh." This close restates the six links of my link round under their own numbers and adds nothing new.

---

## The seed promise (the ground every link stands on)

- [L1] 2 Samuel 7:12: "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom."
- [L2] *qereb* (H7130, "the nearest part... bowels") is the body the seed comes out of.
- [L3] Psalms 132:11: "Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne. [body: Heb. belly]"
- [L3] Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne".
- [L3] Romans 1:3: "which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh".
- [L2] The word in Romans 1:3 is *sperma* (G4690). Its lexicon gloss is "something sown, i.e. seed (including the male 'sperm'); by implication, offspring".
- [L4] The promise is sworn as fruit of a man's loins, "according to the flesh". Footing:
  - 2 Samuel 7:12 with *qereb*;
  - Acts 2:30 and Romans 1:3 with *sperma*.
  
  A seed that proceeds out of the bowels and loins comes down through men's loins. It comes as Hebrews 7:10 says of Levi: "he was yet in the loins of his father".

**The reckoning by the father's house**

- [L1] Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood."
- [L3] Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers".
- [L3] Ezra 2:59: "they could not shew their father's house, and their seed, whether they [were] of Israel: [Addan: also called, Addon] [seed: or, pedigree]".
- [L3] Luke 2:4: "(because he was of the house and lineage of David:)", which is said of Joseph.
- [L4] Footing: Hebrews 7:14 with Numbers 1:18 and Ezra 2:59. The law declares a pedigree "by the house of their fathers". So "evident" descent from Judah is shown through the house of a father. The house the text names is Joseph's, "of the house and lineage of David" (Luke 2:4).

---

## C1: Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal. KEPT.

**What the text calls them**
- [L1] Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband..." The word is *anēr* (G435), "husband, man".
- [L1] Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]". The word for "wife" is *gynē* (G1135), "specially, a wife".
- [L3] Deuteronomy 22:24: "the man, because he hath humbled his neighbour's wife". The word is *ishshah* (H802), "wife". This is said of a betrothed damsel.

**How the canon states begetting**
- [L1] Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the LORD. [Cain: that is, Gotten, or, Acquired]"
- [L2] The verb is *yada* (H3045), whose gloss includes "lie by man".

**The timing rows, read in Matthew's own order**
- [L1] Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- [L3] Matthew 1:24: "took unto him his wife". The verb is *paralambanō* (G3880), "to receive near, i.e. associate with oneself".
- [L3] Deuteronomy 20:7: "what man [is there] that hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her?" This shows that the taking is a separate step from the betrothal.
- [L1] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."
- [L3] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" The verb *ginōskō* (G1097, "know") is in the present tense. It states her condition at the moment the angel spoke.

**[L4] The union.** Footing:
- the seed rows above (2 Samuel 7:12 with *qereb*; Romans 1:3 with *sperma*);
- the means the canon states (Genesis 4:1 with *yada*);
- the marriage from the espousal (Matthew 1:19 *anēr*; Matthew 1:20 *gynē*; Deuteronomy 22:24 *ishshah*).

The chain runs this way:
1. The finding is dated before the taking (Matthew 1:18 and 1:24, with Deuteronomy 20:7).
2. "Knew her not till" covers the pregnancy after the taking (Matthew 1:25).
3. Mary's "I know not a man" is her state when the angel spoke (Luke 1:34).

So Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins.

## C2: Luke 1:37 is a sign drawn from a conception with a named father. KEPT.

- [L1] Luke 1:36-37: "And, behold, thy cousin Elisabeth, she hath also conceived a son in her old age: and this is the sixth month with her, who was called barren. For with God nothing shall be impossible."
- [L2] *syllambanō* (G4815, "to conceive") is the verb in Luke 1:36 and also in Luke 1:31, "thou shalt conceive in thy womb".
- [L3] Luke 1:13: "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John."
- [L4] Footing: Luke 1:36 with *syllambanō*, and Luke 1:13.
  - The sign the angel gives Mary is a conception with Zacharias named as the father, "bear thee a son".
  - "Also conceived" joins Mary's conceiving to that sign with the same verb.
  - In that sign, God's power and a named husband stand in the same conception.

## C3: Isaiah's sign shows a sign-child and a husband together. KEPT.

- [L1] Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel. [shall call: or, thou, O virgin, shalt call]"
- [L3] Isaiah 7:16: "For before the child shall know to refuse the evil, and choose the good, the land that thou abhorrest shall be forsaken of both her kings."
- [L3] Isaiah 8:3: "And I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son. Then said the LORD to me, Call his name Mahershalalhashbaz. [went: Heb. approached]"
- [L3] Isaiah 8:4: "For before the child shall have knowledge to cry, My father, and my mother, the riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria shall be taken away before the king of Assyria. [the riches...: or, he that is before the king of Assyria shall take away the riches, etc]"
- [L3] Isaiah 8:8: "the stretching out of his wings shall fill the breadth of thy land, O Immanuel. [stretching...: Heb. fulness of the breadth of thy land shall be the stretchings out of his wings]"
- [L2] *harah* (H2029, "to be (or become) pregnant, conceive") stands in Isaiah 7:14 and in Isaiah 8:3.
- [L4] Footing: Isaiah 7:14 with *harah*, and Isaiah 7:16 with Isaiah 8:3-4 and 8:8.
  - The sign is bounded by a child's age in Isaiah's own day.
  - In the chapter that follows, the conceiving comes after the husband "approached".
  - The child there cries "My father, and my mother".
  - Matthew 1:22 says "all this was done, that it might be fulfilled". The sign it fulfils joins a conception to a husband.

## C4: The reply of Luke 2:49 leaves "thy father" standing. KEPT.

- [L1] Luke 2:48: "Son, why hast thou thus dealt with us? behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." *Patēr* (G3962, "father") is Mary's own word.
- [L3] Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?"
- [L3] Luke 2:51: "And he went down with them, and came to Nazareth, and was subject unto them".
- [L3] 1 Chronicles 28:6: "Solomon thy son, he shall build my house and my courts: for I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father."
- [L4] Footing: Luke 2:48-49 with *patēr*, and 1 Chronicles 28:6.
  - In one verse, 1 Chronicles 28:6 sets the son David begat ("thy son") beside the son God chose ("my son"). The two fathers stand together.
  - So "my Father's business" (Luke 2:49) stands beside "thy father" (Luke 2:48) without removing it.
  - The child then goes down "subject unto them" (Luke 2:51).

The narrator's word agrees with this reading:
- [L1] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph".
- [L2] The verb is *nomizō* (G3543, "properly, to do by law (usage)"). Its form is the one in Acts 16:13: "where prayer was wont to be made".
- The word reports the reckoning "by the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:2). It carries no verdict of its own.

## C5: The "therefore" of Luke 1:35 reaches back to verse 32. KEPT.

- [L1] Luke 1:32: "He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David".
- [L1] Luke 1:35: "therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- [L2] *kaleō* (G2564, "to call") is the verb of the title in both verses.

The title is a covenant title. Its source text is:
- [L3] 2 Samuel 7:14: "I will be his father, and he shall be my son."

The psalm that speaks of begetting the Son is applied in the New Testament at three occasions:
- [L3] Psalms 2:7: "I will declare the decree: the LORD hath said unto me, Thou [art] my Son; this day have I begotten thee. [the decree: or, for a decree]"
- [L3] Acts 13:33, at the resurrection: "he hath raised up Jesus again; as it is also written in the second psalm, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee."
- [L3] Hebrews 5:5, at the priesthood: "Christ glorified not himself to be made an high priest; but he that said unto him, Thou art my Son, to day have I begotten thee."
- [L3] Hebrews 1:5, beside 2 Samuel 7:14: "Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee? And again, I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son?"

The verbs of Luke 1:35 have their own use elsewhere:
- [L3] Acts 1:8: "after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you". This is power given to the apostles.
- [L3] Luke 9:34: "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them".

[L4] The dio kai ("therefore") in v.35 connects back to v.32, not forward to biological divine paternity. Footing: Luke 1:32 and 1:35, both with *kaleō*, together with 2 Samuel 7:14 and the three applications of Psalms 2:7.
- The title and "the throne of his father David" are given in Luke 1:32, before Mary asks "How shall this be" in Luke 1:34.
- The verbs "come upon" and "overshadow" are presence and power, as Acts 1:8 and Luke 9:34 use them.
- Romans 1:4 joins the title to the resurrection: "declared [to be] the Son of God with power... by the resurrection from the dead: [declared: Gr. determined]". It comes in the same passage as "the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3).

## C6: Joseph's grounds in Matthew 1:19 are two: he is just, and he is unwilling to expose her. KEPT.

- [L1] Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
- [L2] The words of the verse:
  - *dikaios* (G1342, "just");
  - *paradeigmatizō* (G3856, "expose to infamy");
  - *boulomai* (G1014, "be... minded, intend"). This is a verb of intent.
- [L3] Matthew 1:20 gives the angel's answer: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"
- [L3] John 1:13 shows the same "of God" said of believers: "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God."
- [L4] Footing: Matthew 1:19 with *dikaios*, *paradeigmatizō* and *boulomai*, and Matthew 1:20 with John 1:13.
  - The verse states an intent and two grounds.
  - The angel answers the intent with "fear not to take".
  - The row that says "of the Holy Ghost" names "Joseph, thou son of David" as the one who takes his wife and names the child: "thou shalt call his name JESUS" (Matthew 1:21), which is done in Matthew 1:25.
  - "Of the Holy Ghost" stands as "of God" stands in John 1:13. It is the origin God claims as his, and it is held whole with the father named in the same verse.

---

## The record's reading

The scripture keeps the flesh and the covenant title together and lets neither erase the other:
- the seed of David "according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3; Acts 2:30), out of the bowels (2 Samuel 7:12);
- reckoned "by the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:18);
- the father named by the mother ("thy father," Luke 2:48), by the town ("the son of Joseph," John 6:42), by a disciple ("Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph," John 1:45), and by the angel ("Joseph, thou son of David," Matthew 1:20);
- made "in all things... like unto [his] brethren" (Hebrews 2:17), as "he took on [him] the seed of Abraham. [took not...: Gr. taketh not hold of angels, but of the seed of Abraham he taketh hold]" (Hebrews 2:16).

"Son of God" is the covenant and resurrection title of 2 Samuel 7:14 and Psalms 2:7. "Of the Holy Ghost" is the origin God claims, spoken in the same breath as "Joseph, thou son of David."

[L4] Footing: Romans 1:3 with *sperma*, Genesis 4:1 with *yada*, and Matthew 1:19-20 with *anēr* and *gynē*. Christ had a biological father, Joseph, his named father of the house of David. Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the seed of David came, as it was sworn, "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh" (Acts 2:30).
